Przytyk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Przytyk, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Przytyk from the second half of the 17th century; by 1921, 1,205 Jews made up nearly 90% of the village, mostly murdered by Germans in 1942. Przytyk is historically notable for a violent March 9, 1936 antisemitic pogrom. This cemetery, in use no later than 1770 based on surviving tombstones, served not only Przytyk but Białobrzegi (until the 1960s) and Radom (until 1931) as well. Victims of the 1936 pogrom were buried here, commemorated in 1939 with a plaque for victim Josek Minakowski, unveiled before about 2,000 attendees including a Radom Jewish delegation. The cemetery remained in use until the 1942 deportations; in fall 1939, a man named Brojtman, killed by Germans during a forced-labor roundup, was buried here.
